documents.title: AI Syllabus Statements
tiers: Optional addition: AI required for some assignments
documents.summary: TWU's AI Collaborative page offers faculty sample syllabus statements: a student-data protection statement and three tiers of student AI use, plus an optional add-on for requiring AI. It leaves the choice to each instructor and recommends disclosure over bans because violations are hard to detect.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Faculty can create customized AI policies for each course based on their teaching goals' and supplies tiered templates (permissive, mixed-use, unpermitted) rather than one rule, so the stance is delegates.

units.why: The page opens by saying syllabus AI policies 'help set clear expectations for students and protect academic integrity'; it explains why policies are wanted, so it is a rationale (informs) about communicating expectations, typed P09 because it justifies putting AI statements in syllabi.
units.anchor: Adding AI policies to courses helps set clear expectations for students
units.frag_start: Adding AI policies to courses helps
units.fit_note: States the benefit of syllabus statements rather than a requirement to include one; no mandate is stated.

units.why: 'Without clear guidelines, students may be confused... unintentional violations or missed learning opportunities' explains the cost of silence; it is a rationale for clear guidance, nearest to P09 (syllabus statement), not P41 because it is not about skill-building.
units.anchor: students may be confused about what AI use is acceptable

units.fit_note: Rationale for clarity rather than a rule requiring a statement.

units.why: 'Faculty are expected to abide by these restrictions on their own AI use, regardless of whether the statement is included in their syllabus' binds faculty to the data rules whether or not stated; actor instructor, must, about faculty AI use with student data, so P50.

units.why: 'You will be informed about what data (if any) is shared, provided, or stored when we use any AI tool in the classroom' commits the instructor to tell students about data handling when instructors use AI; instructor disclosure to students (P47).

units.why: 'and you can opt out' gives students the right to opt out of AI tool use involving their data in class; a choice guarantee, nearest P51 (AI optional, alternatives) though the opt-out is about data.
